layers.label: U.S. House
layers.rank_note: 6 congressional districts — the largest districts Oregon carries below the state itself

source.answers: The U.S. House district covering the point, and the representative holding it.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Legislative, layer 0 (120th Congressional Districts), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 6 features for Oregon, measured 2026-11-12. Layer 4, the 119th Congress's map, draws the same 6 districts (every intersection-over-union 1.0), so nothing changes on 3 January 2027, and the builder refuses to write if the two differ before then. Simplified by Douglas-Peucker at a 5 m interval and refused over an 8 m fidelity ceiling.

source.people: congress-roster.json, rebuilt weekly by CI from the public-domain unitedstates/congress-legislators dataset — including each member's district office and Washington office.

layers.label: School District (Secondary)
layers.rank_note: 1 secondary district (the Harney County Union High School District, 22,858 km2 of land), running the higher grades over part of the elementary districts' ground, drawn from a mirrored tile archive

source.answers: The secondary school district covering the point, where one runs the higher grades over the point's elementary district.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — School, layer 1 (secondary school districts), mirrored into a vector-tile archive this site serves (scripts/mirror_tiger_tiles.py); 1 feature for Oregon, measured 2026-11-12: the Harney County Union High School District, running grades 9 to 12. The unified districts and the elementary districts together cover the state's land, the unified districts nearly all of it (223,910 and 24,721 km2 of Oregon's 248,631 km2), and the 1 secondary district lies over part of the elementary districts' ground (22,858 km2), so a reader there is in one elementary and one secondary district at once. One unified record is not a district: the Census files coastal water, where no school district reaches, as "School District Not Defined" (GEOID 4199997, 44 km2 of water and no land), and the card says no school district is defined there.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER YET. No list of the districts' school board members was read in this pass — recorded as gap or-school-board-members.
source.applies: Oregon — part of the elementary districts' ground; the layer answers nothing elsewhere.

layers.label: Oregon Senate District
layers.rank_note: 30 Senate districts, each exactly two House districts — larger on average than a county

source.answers: The Senate district covering the point, and the senator it elects.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Legislative, layer 1 (2026 State Legislative Districts - Upper), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 30 features, measured 2026-11-12, identical to the 2024 vintage (layer 5) that day. Every Senate district is exactly two House districts (Senate District N is House Districts 2N-1 and 2N, measured that day), so both chambers are simplified in one shared topology and their lines cannot part. Simplified by Douglas-Peucker at a 5 m interval and refused over an 8 m fidelity ceiling.

source.people: or-senate-members.json, rebuilt weekly by CI from the Legislature's own data service (api.oregonlegislature.gov, the members of its newest regular session): each senator's name, party, Capitol room and telephone, Legislature e-mail address and page.

layers.label: ZIP Code
layers.rank_note: 430 ZIP Code Tabulation Areas that reach into Oregon (575 in the app's bounding box), drawn from a tile archive of the ones inside the state; the layer hides outside it

source.answers: The ZIP Code Tabulation Area covering the point — the Census Bureau's areal approximation of the USPS delivery routes sharing a ZIP code, not a postal boundary.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — ZIP Code Tabulation Areas, layer 11 of the PUMA/TAD/TAZ/UGA/ZCTA service, mirrored into a vector-tile archive of the ZCTAs that reach into Oregon (scripts/mirror_tiger_tiles.py). ZCTAs carry NO STATE FIELD because they cross state lines, so this is the one TIGERweb layer here fetched by a bounding ENVELOPE rather than STATE='41'. The app's box reaches into Washington, Idaho, Nevada and California, and measured 2026-11-12, 430 of the 575 ZCTAs in it reach into Oregon and are kept in the archive.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND NONE IS MISSING: a ZIP code is a mail-routing convenience, not a unit of government, so nobody is elected from one. The card says what the boundary actually is rather than leaving a reader to assume it means more.
source.applies: Oregon. The layer is hidden outside the state outline, because outside it the Census's point query answers with a neighbouring state's real ZIP code.

layers.label: City or Town
layers.rank_note: 241 incorporated cities, drawn from a tile archive mirrored from TIGERweb

source.answers: The incorporated city containing the point, or that the point is outside every one.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Places_CouSub_ConCity_SubMCD, layer 4 (incorporated places), mirrored into a vector-tile archive this site serves (scripts/mirror_tiger_tiles.py); 241 records: 231 cities, 9 towns and the city of Greenhorn, which the Census records as an inactive government, measured 2026-11-12. MOST OF OREGON IS IN NO INCORPORATED CITY (about 1% of its land, 2,628.5 of 248,630.8 km2, is inside one), and there the county is the general-purpose local government, so an empty card says the point is outside every one rather than naming a place. Oregon's 9 towns are incorporated like its cities and are drawn with them. The Census's census-designated places and county subdivisions are statistical areas with no government and are not drawn.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER YET. No statewide roster of Oregon's mayors and councils was read in this pass; the card names the place and links nothing it has not verified. Recorded as gap or-municipal-officeholders.

layers.label: Police Station
layers.rank_note: nearest police stations by straight-line distance — a point layer, ranked with the other nearest-N layers

source.answers: The three nearest police stations to the point, by straight-line distance, with each one's address.

boundary.label: USGS The National Map — structures layer 53 (Police Stations), queried live at runtime by a bounding envelope through the paged loader. Public domain. Measured 2026-11-12: 281 points in Oregon's envelope, which reaches into Washington, Idaho, Nevada and California; the service caps a page at 2,000 records, so the loader pages if that is ever reached.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND NONE IS MISSING: a police station is a facility, not an elected district. Nobody is elected from one.
source.applies: Oregon — plus the border strip its envelope necessarily includes. A BUILDING, NOT A JURISDICTION: which agency answers at a given point is a service-area question this instance has not been researched for, so the card says where the nearest are and never who serves you. Nearest-three is a proximity fact, so for a reader near the state line the nearest one really may be in a neighbouring state, and the card's intro says these are straight-line distances.

anchor_point.note: Oregon State Capitol, 900 Court Street NE, Salem, Marion County

negative_point.note: The Pacific about 30 km off Lincoln City — outside Oregon and outside every other instance in the fleet, and inside permalink_gate so the app answers the click and every shipped layer correctly returns nothing. Measured 2026-11-12: TIGERweb's state layer names no state here (control: the State Capitol returns Oregon), none of the state's shipped boundary files contains it, and no outline in fleet-outlines.json does, nor any of the other batch-3 states' outlines. IT IS OPEN WATER, SO NO NEIGHBOUR'S GO-LIVE MOVES IT.

geometry.note: The whole-Oregon outline for the coverage wash (loadMetroOutline), dissolved from the county fabric (36 counties).
Oregon's 36 counties — the instance's offline anchor layer and the ground the coverage tests use.
The 6 U.S. House districts, TIGERweb layer 0 (CD120), the same map as layer 4 (CD119).
The 30 Oregon Senate districts, TIGERweb layer 1 (2026 State Legislative Districts - Upper), simplified in one topology with the House districts.
The 60 Oregon House districts, TIGERweb layer 2 (2026 State Legislative Districts - Lower), simplified in one topology with the Senate districts.

The ZIP code search index (scripts/build_zip_index.mjs): one Point per ZIP code the app's ZIP layer draws, at the spot inside it on the layer's own ground farthest from every edge, with its extent and its layer, so a ZIP code typed into the search box selects that spot, turns the ZIP layer on and pins it for comparison (ENGINE geocoder-search, showZip). A ZIP code with no spot 75 m clear of every edge is left out, and one that crosses into another app's state is listed by whichever app holds more of it. GENERATED from data/app/tiles/zip-code.pmtiles, with each spot inside metro-outline.json (the outline its coverage test reads); --check rebuilds it from the committed archive and outline. Exact count, because it changes only when the Census Bureau changes its ZIP Code Tabulation Areas, and that wants reading rather than a widened bound.

The officers Oregon elects statewide and its two U.S. senators: state, officers (office, name, the office's own website, the day the name was last checked there) and usSenate. Built weekly by scripts/build_statewide_officials.py from or/data/source/statewide-officials.source.json, which lists each office, the name and the page that must print it; the build reads robots.txt before every page, refuses to write when a page it read no longer prints the name, keeps the last checked record when a page cannot be read, and takes the senators from senate.gov's own list. Network-first: a name can change.
